unit.title: Đọc B2 (mở rộng)
unit.summary: Vườn trên mái nhà, học ngoại ngữ khi trưởng thành, thời trang nhanh, thói quen, khoa học công dân, tuần làm bốn ngày, vi nhựa, trì hoãn, du lịch quá tải, rác vũ trụ.

lessons.title: Vườn trên mái nhà
lessons.summary: Trồng rau giữa lòng thành phố.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: In many crowded cities, flat rooftops were once used for little more than air-conditioning units and water tanks. Today, a growing number of them are being turned into vegetable gardens, run by residents, schools and even restaurants.
paragraphs.vi: Ở nhiều thành phố đông đúc, mái nhà bằng từng chỉ dùng để đặt máy điều hoà và bồn nước. Ngày nay, ngày càng nhiều mái được biến thành vườn rau do cư dân, trường học, thậm chí nhà hàng vận hành.

paragraphs.en: The advantages go beyond fresh tomatoes. Plants absorb heat, so a green roof can keep the floors below noticeably cooler in summer and reduce electricity bills. Gardens also slow down rainwater, which helps prevent streets from flooding during heavy storms.
paragraphs.vi: Lợi ích không chỉ là cà chua tươi. Cây hấp thụ nhiệt nên mái xanh có thể giữ các tầng bên dưới mát hơn rõ rệt vào mùa hè và giảm tiền điện. Vườn cũng làm chậm dòng nước mưa, giúp đường phố đỡ ngập khi mưa lớn.

paragraphs.en: However, rooftop gardening is not as simple as it looks. Soil and water are heavy, so engineers must first check that a building can carry the extra weight. Strong winds and intense sunlight also make some crops difficult to grow.
paragraphs.vi: Tuy vậy, làm vườn trên mái không đơn giản như vẻ ngoài. Đất và nước rất nặng nên kỹ sư phải kiểm tra trước xem toà nhà có chịu được trọng lượng thêm không. Gió mạnh và nắng gắt cũng khiến một số loại cây khó trồng.

paragraphs.en: Even so, many participants say the biggest reward is social: neighbors who had never spoken now meet every weekend to water, weed and share the harvest.
paragraphs.vi: Dù vậy, nhiều người tham gia nói phần thưởng lớn nhất là về mặt xã hội: hàng xóm chưa từng nói chuyện nay gặp nhau mỗi cuối tuần để tưới cây, nhổ cỏ và chia nhau thu hoạch.

headings: Practical difficulties of farming high above the street
From neglected space to growing space
Benefits for buildings and streets, not only for the kitchen
A shared garden that brings neighbors together
How restaurants profit from selling rooftop vegetables
Choosing the right crops for a sunny roof
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 describes rooftops changing from places for machines into vegetable gardens; paragraph 2 lists benefits beyond food (cooler floors, lower bills, less flooding); paragraph 3 explains the difficulties (weight, wind, sunlight); paragraph 4 says the biggest reward is social. Restaurants are only mentioned as one type of gardener, and crops that are hard to grow are only one detail in paragraph 3.

exercises.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Rooftop gardens are spreading in cities and bring practical and social benefits, though they are not easy to set up.
Rooftop gardens are usually too heavy and too windy to be safe on most city buildings today.
Growing vegetables on roofs has become the cheapest and quickest way to feed a whole city.
Restaurants have led the rise of rooftop gardens because they want to sell fresh local food.
exercises.explain: The passage moves from the spread of rooftop gardens (paragraph 1) to their benefits (paragraph 2), their difficulties (paragraph 3) and their social reward (paragraph 4). The other choices exaggerate one detail or add claims the passage never makes.

exercises.prompt: How can a green roof reduce electricity bills?
choices: By producing solar power
By storing rainwater for washing
By keeping the floors below cooler
By replacing air-conditioning units
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: plants absorb heat, so the floors below stay noticeably cooler in summer and electricity bills fall.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 2, the word "absorb" is closest in meaning to …
choices: release
produce
take in
measure
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: "Plants absorb heat, so a green roof can keep the floors below noticeably cooler" — the plants take in the heat, which keeps the rooms below cool.

exercises.prompt: What can be inferred from paragraph 4 about many of the neighbors before they started gardening?
choices: They had argued about how the roof should be used.
They hardly knew each other.
They already met every weekend for other activities.
They had worked as professional gardeners.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: "neighbors who had never spoken now meet every weekend", so before the gardens many of them did not know each other. Nothing suggests arguments or professional experience.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer begin paragraph 3 with "However"?
choices: To change the topic from city roofs to farms in the countryside
To disagree with the people who run rooftop gardens
To show that green roofs do not really cool buildings
To introduce the difficulties after describing the advantages
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2 lists advantages; paragraph 3 starts with "However" to turn to the problems: weight, strong winds and intense sunlight. The writer does not deny the cooling effect or criticize the gardeners.

exercises.statement: Rooftop gardens can help reduce flooding in the streets.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: gardens slow down rainwater, which helps prevent streets from flooding during heavy storms.

exercises.statement: Rooftop gardens produce more vegetables than farms of the same size.
exercises.explain: The passage never compares how much rooftop gardens produce with what farms produce.

exercises.prompt: Many participants say the biggest reward is ___.
choices: social
financial
medical
exercises.explain: Câu cuối: "the biggest reward is social" — hàng xóm gặp gỡ, chia nhau thu hoạch.

exercises.text: Flat city roofs that once had almost no purpose are increasingly being ___ into vegetable plots. Apart from food, these gardens keep the rooms underneath cooler and help prevent ___ in the streets. Before anything is planted, engineers must confirm that the building can bear the additional ___. For many gardeners, however, the greatest benefit is that former ___ now meet regularly to work together.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: rooftops are being "turned into" gardens; paragraph 2: gardens help prevent streets from flooding; paragraph 3: engineers check that the building "can carry the extra weight"; paragraph 4: neighbors "who had never spoken" now meet every weekend.

lessons.title: Học ngoại ngữ khi đã lớn
lessons.summary: Người lớn có thật sự học ngoại ngữ kém hơn trẻ em?

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

blocks.title: Learning a Language as an Adult

paragraphs.en: It is often said that children learn languages effortlessly while adults struggle. There is some truth in this: young children who grow up hearing a language usually develop a native-like accent, something most adult learners never fully achieve.
paragraphs.vi: Người ta thường nói trẻ em học ngôn ngữ dễ dàng còn người lớn thì chật vật. Điều này có phần đúng: trẻ nhỏ lớn lên khi nghe một ngôn ngữ thường có giọng như người bản xứ, điều mà hầu hết người học trưởng thành không bao giờ đạt được trọn vẹn.

paragraphs.en: However, adults have advantages of their own. They can understand grammar rules when these are explained, use strategies such as making flashcards, and connect new words to knowledge they already have. In the first months of study, adults often make faster progress than children.
paragraphs.vi: Tuy nhiên, người lớn có lợi thế riêng. Họ hiểu được quy tắc ngữ pháp khi được giải thích, dùng các chiến lược như làm thẻ ghi nhớ và liên kết từ mới với kiến thức sẵn có. Trong vài tháng đầu, người lớn thường tiến bộ nhanh hơn trẻ em.

paragraphs.en: The real difference may be time and exposure. A child hears the language for many hours every day, whereas an adult might study for two hours a week after work. When adults are surrounded by a language, for example after moving abroad, they can reach a very high level.
paragraphs.vi: Khác biệt thật sự có lẽ là thời gian và mức độ tiếp xúc. Trẻ nghe ngôn ngữ nhiều giờ mỗi ngày, còn người lớn có thể chỉ học hai giờ mỗi tuần sau giờ làm. Khi người lớn được bao quanh bởi ngôn ngữ, chẳng hạn sau khi ra nước ngoài sống, họ có thể đạt trình độ rất cao.

paragraphs.en: So if you are starting later in life, the message is encouraging: regular practice matters far more than your age.
paragraphs.vi: Vậy nếu bạn bắt đầu muộn, thông điệp rất đáng khích lệ: luyện tập đều đặn quan trọng hơn nhiều so với tuổi tác.

headings: An encouraging message for late starters
The grain of truth in a popular belief
Strengths that adult learners bring
Hours of contact: the real gap between children and adults
Why flashcards work better than textbooks
The best age to move abroad
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 admits that the popular belief is partly true (accent); paragraph 2 lists adults' advantages; paragraph 3 says the real difference is time and exposure; paragraph 4 gives an encouraging conclusion for people who start late. Flashcards are only one example in paragraph 2, and the passage never names a best age to move abroad.

exercises.prompt: Which statement best expresses the writer's main argument?
choices: Children are better than adults at every part of language learning, especially grammar.
Adults should focus on grammar rules and accept that their accent will never improve.
Moving abroad is the only realistic way for an adult to learn a foreign language well.
Adults can learn a language very well if they get enough regular practice and exposure.
exercises.explain: Paragraphs 2–4 argue that adults have their own strengths, that the real difference is time and exposure, and that regular practice matters more than age. Moving abroad is only an example in paragraph 3, and paragraph 2 contradicts the idea that children are better at everything.

exercises.prompt: What do young children usually achieve that most adults do not?
choices: A larger vocabulary
Better spelling
Faster progress in the first months
A native-like accent
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: children who grow up hearing a language usually develop a native-like accent, which most adult learners never fully achieve.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 3, the word "exposure" is closest in meaning to …
choices: danger
contact with the language
public attention
explanation of rules
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: a child "hears the language for many hours every day" — exposure here means how much contact a learner has with the language, not danger or public attention.

exercises.prompt: What does the passage suggest about the popular belief that children simply learn languages better?
choices: It contains some truth, but the difference may come mostly from time and exposure.
It is completely false, because adults always learn faster than children.
It is true for grammar but not for accent.
It shows that age matters more than regular practice.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 says there is "some truth" in the belief (accent), but paragraph 3 says the real difference "may be time and exposure". Adults are faster only in the first months (paragraph 2), and paragraph 4 says practice matters more than age.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer mention adults who move abroad in paragraph 3?
choices: To recommend that every adult learner should leave their country
To explain why children develop better accents than adults
To show that adults can reach a high level when they have plenty of exposure
To argue that studying after work is a waste of time
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: moving abroad is an example of adults being "surrounded by a language", after which "they can reach a very high level". It supports the point about exposure; it is not a recommendation for everyone.

exercises.statement: Adults often progress faster than children at the beginning.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: in the first months of study, adults often make faster progress than children.

exercises.statement: Flashcards are the most effective learning strategy.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2 only mentions flashcards as one strategy; it never says which strategy is the most effective.

exercises.prompt: Regular practice matters far more than your ___.
choices: age
accent
teacher
exercises.explain: Câu cuối: "regular practice matters far more than your age".

exercises.text: People often believe adults are poor language learners, and it is true that few adults ever sound like ___ speakers. However, adults can make sense of grammar explanations and use study ___, so they often move ahead faster at first. The key difference seems to be how much ___ each group has with the language. The lesson for late starters is not to worry about their ___, as long as they keep practicing.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: most adults never fully achieve a "native-like accent"; paragraph 2: adults use "strategies such as making flashcards"; paragraph 3: the real difference is time and exposure (contact with the language); paragraph 4: regular practice matters far more than age.

lessons.title: Thời trang nhanh
lessons.summary: Quần áo rẻ và cái giá ẩn phía sau.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

blocks.title: The Hidden Cost of Fast Fashion

paragraphs.en: Fast fashion refers to clothing that is designed, produced and sold very quickly, so that shops can offer new styles almost every week. Prices are low, and shoppers are encouraged to buy often and replace items before they wear out.
paragraphs.vi: Thời trang nhanh chỉ quần áo được thiết kế, sản xuất và bán rất nhanh để cửa hàng có mẫu mới gần như mỗi tuần. Giá rẻ và người mua được khuyến khích mua thường xuyên, thay đồ trước khi chúng cũ.

paragraphs.en: This business model has a significant environmental cost. Making clothes requires huge amounts of water and energy, and many cheap garments are made from synthetic fibers that do not break down easily. A large share of these clothes ends up in landfills after being worn only a few times.
paragraphs.vi: Mô hình kinh doanh này gây tổn hại môi trường đáng kể. Làm quần áo cần lượng nước và năng lượng khổng lồ, và nhiều quần áo rẻ làm từ sợi tổng hợp khó phân huỷ. Phần lớn số quần áo này bị đưa ra bãi rác sau khi chỉ mặc vài lần.

paragraphs.en: There are also concerns about working conditions. To keep prices down, some factories pay very low wages and require long hours, and workers may have little protection if they are injured.
paragraphs.vi: Cũng có lo ngại về điều kiện làm việc. Để giữ giá thấp, một số nhà máy trả lương rất thấp, bắt làm nhiều giờ và công nhân có thể ít được bảo vệ nếu bị thương.

paragraphs.en: Consumers can make a difference. Buying fewer but better-made items, choosing second-hand clothes and repairing what we already own all reduce demand for disposable fashion.
paragraphs.vi: Người tiêu dùng có thể tạo ra thay đổi. Mua ít hơn nhưng chất lượng hơn, chọn đồ cũ và sửa đồ mình đã có đều làm giảm nhu cầu với thời trang dùng một lần.

headings: What shoppers can do to slow the trend
Damage to the natural world
Clothes made fast and sold cheap
The human cost inside factories
Why second-hand shops are becoming fashionable
How designers invent a new style every week
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 defines fast fashion (quick production, low prices, frequent buying); paragraph 2 describes the environmental cost; paragraph 3 the working conditions; paragraph 4 what consumers can do. Second-hand clothes are only one suggestion in paragraph 4, and the passage never explains how designers work.

exercises.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
choices: How fast-fashion companies manage to design and deliver new styles every week
The environmental and human costs of cheap, quickly made clothes, and how buyers can help
Why clothes made from synthetic fibers are better value than clothes made from natural ones
How clothing factories have improved wages and working hours in recent years
exercises.explain: Paragraphs 2 and 3 describe the environmental and human costs, and paragraph 4 says what consumers can do. Weekly styles are only part of the definition in paragraph 1, and the passage says nothing positive about synthetic fibers or factory conditions.

exercises.prompt: Why are many cheap garments a problem for the environment?
choices: They are too heavy and bulky to transport over long distances.
They are made from fibers that do not break down easily.
They contain dangerous colors that harm the people who wear them.
They cannot be sold again in second-hand shops later.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: many cheap garments are made from synthetic fibers that do not break down easily, and a large share ends up in landfills.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 4, the word "disposable" is closest in meaning to …
choices: easy to find in many shops
very popular with young people
meant to be thrown away soon
too expensive for most buyers
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: "disposable fashion" refers to the clothes described earlier, which are replaced before they wear out and thrown away after a few wears (paragraphs 1–2).

exercises.prompt: Which of the following would the writer most likely approve of?
choices: Buying a new outfit for every party
Choosing the cheapest shirt in the shop
Throwing away clothes once they go out of style
Having a favorite jacket repaired instead of buying a new one
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4 recommends "repairing what we already own" and buying fewer items. The other choices increase demand for fast fashion, which the writer criticizes in paragraphs 1–3.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer describe factory conditions in paragraph 3?
choices: To show that cheap clothing has a cost for people as well as for the environment
To explain how factories manage to produce clothes so quickly
To argue that every clothing factory in the world is dangerous
To suggest that factory workers should buy fewer clothes
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3 opens with "There are also concerns about working conditions": after the environmental cost (paragraph 2), the writer adds a human cost — low wages, long hours and little protection. It says "some factories", not every factory.

exercises.statement: Fast-fashion clothes are usually worn for many years.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: a large share of these clothes is thrown away after being worn only a few times, and paragraph 1 says shoppers replace items before they wear out.

exercises.statement: Most fast-fashion factories are located in one country.
exercises.explain: The passage does not say where the factories are.

exercises.prompt: Some factories pay very low ___ and require long hours.
choices: wages
taxes
prices
exercises.explain: Đoạn 3: "pay very low wages and require long hours".

exercises.text: Fast fashion depends on producing new designs quickly and selling them at low ___, so people are tempted to shop often. Production uses huge amounts of water and energy, and many cheap garments end up in ___ after only a few wears. In some factories, staff receive low wages, work long hours and are poorly ___ if they are injured. Shoppers can cut demand by buying better-quality clothes, choosing used items and ___ the clothes they already have.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: prices are low and shoppers buy often; paragraph 2: many clothes end up in landfills after a few wears; paragraph 3: workers may have little protection if they are injured; paragraph 4: repairing (mending) what we already own reduces demand.

lessons.title: Thói quen hình thành thế nào
lessons.summary: Vòng lặp tín hiệu – hành động – phần thưởng.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: Much of what we do every day happens without conscious thought. We brush our teeth, check our phones and take the same route to work almost automatically. These behaviors are habits, and psychologists believe they follow a simple pattern.
paragraphs.vi: Phần lớn việc ta làm hằng ngày diễn ra mà không cần suy nghĩ có ý thức. Ta đánh răng, xem điện thoại và đi cùng một tuyến đường đi làm gần như tự động. Những hành vi này là thói quen và các nhà tâm lý học tin rằng chúng theo một mô hình đơn giản.

paragraphs.en: First, there is a cue, such as a time of day, a place or a feeling. The cue triggers a routine, which is the behavior itself. Finally, there is a reward, something pleasant that makes the brain want to repeat the routine the next time the cue appears.
paragraphs.vi: Đầu tiên là tín hiệu, như một thời điểm trong ngày, một nơi chốn hay một cảm xúc. Tín hiệu kích hoạt hành động lặp lại, tức chính hành vi đó. Cuối cùng là phần thưởng, điều dễ chịu khiến não muốn lặp lại hành động khi tín hiệu xuất hiện lần sau.

paragraphs.en: Understanding this loop can help people change. Instead of relying on willpower alone, it is often more effective to keep the same cue and reward but replace the routine. Someone who snacks when bored, for instance, might go for a short walk instead.
paragraphs.vi: Hiểu vòng lặp này giúp con người thay đổi. Thay vì chỉ dựa vào ý chí, cách hiệu quả hơn thường là giữ nguyên tín hiệu và phần thưởng nhưng thay hành động. Chẳng hạn người hay ăn vặt khi chán có thể đi bộ một chút thay vào đó.

paragraphs.en: New habits take time to form, so small, consistent steps usually work better than dramatic changes.
paragraphs.vi: Thói quen mới cần thời gian để hình thành nên những bước nhỏ, đều đặn thường hiệu quả hơn thay đổi đột ngột.

headings: The three stages of the habit loop
Swapping the behavior while keeping the trigger
Everyday actions we perform without thinking
Patience and small steps
Why willpower is the key to change
How the brain stores long-term memories
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: many daily actions are automatic habits; paragraph 2: cue, routine and reward; paragraph 3: change the routine but keep the cue and reward; paragraph 4: new habits take time, so small steps work best. Paragraph 3 says willpower alone is less effective, and memory is not discussed.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence best summarizes the passage?
choices: Most habits are harmful, so people should use strong willpower to remove them quickly.
Psychologists still disagree strongly about how and why everyday habits are formed.
Habits follow a cue–routine–reward pattern, and knowing it can help people change gradually.
Snacking when bored is the most common bad habit, and walking is the only cure for it.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2 describes the cue–routine–reward loop, paragraph 3 explains how understanding it helps people change, and paragraph 4 recommends small, consistent steps. The passage does not say most habits are harmful, and the snacking example is only an illustration.

exercises.prompt: What is the correct order of the habit loop?
choices: Cue, routine, reward
Routine, reward, cue
Reward, cue, routine
Cue, reward, routine
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: first there is a cue, which triggers a routine, and finally there is a reward.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 2, the word "triggers" is closest in meaning to …
choices: prevents
rewards
repeats
sets off
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: "The cue triggers a routine" — the cue starts the behavior, so triggers means sets off.

exercises.prompt: In the example in paragraph 3, what is most likely the cue?
choices: Going for a short walk
Feeling bored
Eating the snack
Feeling full after eating
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2 says a cue can be a feeling, and paragraph 3 describes someone "who snacks when bored": boredom comes first and starts the routine. Eating the snack is the old routine, and the walk is the new routine.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer mention brushing teeth and checking phones in paragraph 1?
choices: To give familiar examples of things people do almost automatically
To warn readers that checking phones too often is harmful
To show that all habits are healthy
To compare good routines with bad ones
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: these are examples of behaviors that happen "almost automatically", without conscious thought. The writer does not judge them as good or bad.

exercises.statement: Dramatic changes are usually better than small steps.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: small, consistent steps usually work better than dramatic changes.

exercises.statement: It takes exactly 21 days to form a new habit.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4 only says that new habits take time to form; it gives no number of days.

exercises.prompt: Someone who snacks when bored might go for a short ___ instead.
choices: walk
nap
drive
exercises.explain: Đoạn 3: "might go for a short walk instead".

exercises.text: Many of our daily actions are performed ___, without deliberate thought. According to psychologists, each habit begins with a signal, continues with the behavior itself and ends with a pleasant ___ that makes us want to do it again. To break a bad habit, it often works better to ___ only the behavior than to depend on willpower. Because new habits develop slowly, ___ steps tend to succeed more than sudden changes.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: behaviors happen "almost automatically"; paragraph 2: a reward makes the brain want to repeat the routine; paragraph 3: keep the cue and reward but replace (swap) the routine; paragraph 4: small, consistent steps work better than dramatic changes.

lessons.title: Khoa học công dân
lessons.summary: Người bình thường góp dữ liệu cho nghiên cứu.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: Not all scientific research is carried out by professionals in laboratories. In citizen science projects, ordinary volunteers help collect or analyze data, often using nothing more than a smartphone and a few minutes of their free time.
paragraphs.vi: Không phải mọi nghiên cứu khoa học đều do chuyên gia thực hiện trong phòng thí nghiệm. Trong các dự án khoa học công dân, tình nguyện viên bình thường giúp thu thập hoặc phân tích dữ liệu, thường chỉ cần một chiếc điện thoại và vài phút rảnh.

paragraphs.en: The range of projects is remarkably wide. Volunteers count birds in their gardens, photograph insects, record the dates when local trees blossom, or classify images of distant galaxies online. Because thousands of people take part, researchers can gather information across areas far larger than any small team could cover.
paragraphs.vi: Phạm vi dự án rộng đáng kinh ngạc. Tình nguyện viên đếm chim trong vườn, chụp ảnh côn trùng, ghi lại ngày cây ở địa phương ra hoa hay phân loại ảnh các thiên hà xa xôi trên mạng. Vì hàng nghìn người tham gia, nhà nghiên cứu thu thập được thông tin trên những vùng rộng hơn nhiều so với một nhóm nhỏ có thể bao quát.

paragraphs.en: Of course, data collected by non-experts can contain mistakes. To deal with this, projects typically provide training materials, ask several volunteers to check the same item, and use statistical methods to identify unusual results.
paragraphs.vi: Dĩ nhiên dữ liệu do người không chuyên thu thập có thể có sai sót. Để xử lý, các dự án thường cung cấp tài liệu hướng dẫn, nhờ nhiều tình nguyện viên kiểm tra cùng một mục và dùng phương pháp thống kê để phát hiện kết quả bất thường.

paragraphs.en: Participants benefit too. Many say they notice nature more closely and feel a sense of purpose in contributing to real discoveries. In this way, citizen science not only produces knowledge but also brings science closer to the public.
paragraphs.vi: Người tham gia cũng được lợi. Nhiều người nói họ quan sát thiên nhiên kỹ hơn và thấy có mục đích khi góp phần vào những khám phá thật. Như vậy, khoa học công dân không chỉ tạo ra tri thức mà còn đưa khoa học đến gần công chúng hơn.

headings: Ways to keep amateur data reliable
Research that is not only for professionals
A wide variety of tasks on a huge scale
What volunteers gain in return
Why scientists prefer to work in laboratories
Paying the public to collect data
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 introduces volunteers doing research outside laboratories; paragraph 2 shows the range of projects and the large areas covered; paragraph 3 explains how projects deal with mistakes; paragraph 4 describes the benefits for participants and the public. Payment and a preference for laboratories are never mentioned.

exercises.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Data collected by volunteers contains so many mistakes that scientists cannot use it.
Smartphones have now replaced laboratories as the main place where science happens.
Ordinary volunteers make useful contributions to research, and they benefit from taking part too.
Most new discoveries are now made by members of the public without help from scientists.
exercises.explain: The passage explains how volunteers help collect and analyze data (paragraphs 1–2), how mistakes are handled (paragraph 3) and how participants benefit (paragraph 4). Paragraph 3 says errors can be managed, so the data is not useless.

exercises.prompt: What is the main advantage of having thousands of volunteers?
choices: Research becomes free.
Mistakes disappear completely.
Professional scientists are no longer needed.
Data can be gathered across very large areas.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: because thousands of people take part, researchers can gather information across areas far larger than any small team could cover.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 2, the word "remarkably" is closest in meaning to …
choices: slightly
surprisingly
officially
recently
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: "The range of projects is remarkably wide" — the examples, from birds to galaxies, show that the range is surprisingly (unusually) wide.

exercises.prompt: Why do projects probably ask several volunteers to check the same item?
choices: Because each volunteer is paid a small fee for every item checked
Because there are too few items for every volunteer to have their own
Because scientists want to test how well the volunteers remember things
Because an answer several people agree on is more likely to be correct
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3 lists this as a way to deal with mistakes in non-expert data: if several people independently give the same answer, it is less likely to be an error. The passage mentions no payment and no shortage of items.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer mention counting birds and classifying galaxies?
choices: To show how wide the range of projects is
To show that volunteers need expensive equipment
To suggest that astronomy projects are the most popular
To explain how volunteers are trained
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2 begins "The range of projects is remarkably wide" and then gives these very different examples to support that point.

exercises.statement: Some citizen science tasks can be done without going outdoors.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: volunteers can "classify images of distant galaxies online", which does not require going outside.

exercises.statement: Most citizen science volunteers are retired people.
exercises.explain: The passage does not mention the age of the volunteers.

exercises.prompt: Citizen science brings science closer to the ___.
choices: public
laboratory
government
exercises.explain: Câu cuối: "brings science closer to the public".

exercises.text: In citizen science, members of the public help researchers by gathering or examining ___, often with nothing more than a phone. Because so many people take part, studies can cover much larger ___ than a small professional team could. Since volunteers may make errors, projects provide ___, have several people review each item and use statistics to spot strange results. Participants say they observe nature more closely and feel that their work has a real ___.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: volunteers collect or analyze data; paragraph 2: they cover areas far larger than a small team could; paragraph 3: projects provide training materials; paragraph 4: participants feel "a sense of purpose".

lessons.title: Tuần làm việc bốn ngày
lessons.summary: Làm ít ngày hơn có giảm năng suất?

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: For most of the last century, a five-day, forty-hour week has been the standard for office workers. Recently, however, a number of companies have experimented with a four-day week, in which employees work fewer hours for the same salary.
paragraphs.vi: Trong phần lớn thế kỷ trước, tuần làm năm ngày, bốn mươi giờ là chuẩn mực của nhân viên văn phòng. Tuy nhiên gần đây, một số công ty đã thử nghiệm tuần làm bốn ngày, nhân viên làm ít giờ hơn với cùng mức lương.

paragraphs.en: The results of these trials have often been surprising. Many firms report that productivity stayed the same or even improved, because staff wasted less time in unnecessary meetings and returned to work feeling rested. Employees also reported lower stress and found it easier to balance work with family responsibilities.
paragraphs.vi: Kết quả các cuộc thử nghiệm thường gây bất ngờ. Nhiều công ty cho biết năng suất giữ nguyên hoặc thậm chí tăng vì nhân viên ít lãng phí thời gian vào các cuộc họp không cần thiết và quay lại làm việc khi đã được nghỉ ngơi. Nhân viên cũng cho biết ít căng thẳng hơn và dễ cân bằng công việc với trách nhiệm gia đình hơn.

paragraphs.en: Nevertheless, the model does not suit every industry. Hospitals, shops and public transport must operate every day, so a shorter week for each worker may require hiring additional staff. Some employees also find that squeezing their work into four days makes those days more intense.
paragraphs.vi: Tuy vậy, mô hình này không phù hợp với mọi ngành. Bệnh viện, cửa hàng và giao thông công cộng phải hoạt động hằng ngày, nên tuần ngắn hơn cho mỗi người có thể đòi hỏi tuyển thêm nhân sự. Một số nhân viên cũng thấy dồn việc vào bốn ngày khiến những ngày đó căng thẳng hơn.

paragraphs.en: The debate is therefore less about whether a four-day week is good or bad and more about how work can be organized more intelligently, whatever the number of days.
paragraphs.vi: Vì thế cuộc tranh luận không hẳn là tuần bốn ngày tốt hay xấu, mà là làm sao tổ chức công việc thông minh hơn, bất kể số ngày là bao nhiêu.

headings: Limits and drawbacks of a shorter week
A challenge to a long-standing working pattern
Trial results that surprised many
The bigger question behind the debate
Why governments are making the four-day week law
Cutting the number of unnecessary meetings
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: the five-day week was standard, but companies are testing four days; paragraph 2: the trials gave surprisingly good results; paragraph 3: the model does not suit every industry or every worker; paragraph 4: the real question is how to organize work. Meetings are only one reason in paragraph 2, and laws are never mentioned.

exercises.prompt: What is the writer's overall view of the four-day week?
choices: It works so well that it should replace the five-day week in every industry soon.
It lowers productivity so much that the companies testing it should give it up.
It can bring real benefits but does not suit every job, and better organization matters most.
It mainly helps employers save money, while employees end up feeling more stressed.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2 reports benefits, paragraph 3 says the model "does not suit every industry", and paragraph 4 says the debate is really about organizing work more intelligently. Paragraph 2 contradicts the claims about lower productivity and more stress.

exercises.prompt: Why did productivity often stay the same during the trials?
choices: Staff wasted less time in meetings and felt rested.
Employees took shorter lunch breaks to finish their work.
Companies hired more managers to check the staff's work.
Salaries were increased to keep the staff motivated.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: staff wasted less time in unnecessary meetings and returned to work feeling rested.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 3, the word "squeezing" is closest in meaning to …
choices: spreading out over more time
pressing into a smaller space
handing over to other people
putting off until a later day
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: "squeezing their work into four days makes those days more intense" — the same work is pressed into less time, so each day is busier.

exercises.prompt: Why might a four-day week be easier to introduce in an office than in a hospital?
choices: Office workers usually earn lower salaries than hospital staff.
Hospitals hold far more unnecessary meetings than offices.
Office work is never as intense as work in a hospital.
An office does not usually need to stay open every day of the week.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 describes the five-day week of office workers, while paragraph 3 says hospitals "must operate every day", so a shorter week there may require more staff. The passage does not compare salaries, meetings or intensity between the two.

exercises.prompt: What is the purpose of the final paragraph?
choices: To move the focus from the number of days to how work is organized
To conclude that the four-day week has failed in most of the trials
To give more examples of companies whose trials were very successful
To list the industries that should not try the four-day week at all
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: the debate is "less about whether a four-day week is good or bad and more about how work can be organized more intelligently, whatever the number of days".

exercises.statement: Every employee finds the four-day week less intense.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: some employees find that squeezing their work into four days makes those days more intense.

exercises.statement: The four-day week is now required by law in some countries.
exercises.explain: The passage does not mention any laws.

exercises.prompt: The debate is really about how work can be organized more ___.
choices: intelligently
cheaply
quickly
exercises.explain: Câu cuối: "how work can be organized more intelligently".

exercises.text: For decades, office staff have normally worked five days a week, but some firms have tested a shorter week with no cut in ___. Many found that output did not fall, partly because employees spent less time in pointless ___ and came back refreshed. Staff also felt less ___ and could handle family duties more easily. However, services that run every day may have to hire extra ___, and some employees find their remaining days more intense.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: employees work fewer hours "for the same salary"; paragraph 2: staff wasted less time in unnecessary meetings and reported lower stress; paragraph 3: services that operate every day may need to hire additional staff.

lessons.title: Vi nhựa
lessons.summary: Những mảnh nhựa nhỏ có mặt khắp nơi.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: Microplastics are pieces of plastic smaller than five millimeters. Some are manufactured at that size, such as the tiny beads once common in face scrubs, but most are created when larger items like bottles and bags slowly break apart under sunlight and waves.
paragraphs.vi: Vi nhựa là mảnh nhựa nhỏ hơn năm milimét. Một số được sản xuất sẵn ở kích cỡ đó, như hạt li ti từng phổ biến trong sữa rửa mặt tẩy da chết, nhưng phần lớn hình thành khi đồ lớn như chai, túi dần vỡ ra dưới ánh nắng và sóng biển.

paragraphs.en: Because they are so small and light, microplastics travel easily. Researchers have found them in deep ocean trenches, on remote mountain tops and in drinking water. Washing synthetic clothes is another source, as each wash can release thousands of fibers into wastewater.
paragraphs.vi: Vì rất nhỏ và nhẹ nên vi nhựa di chuyển dễ dàng. Các nhà nghiên cứu đã tìm thấy chúng ở rãnh đại dương sâu, trên đỉnh núi hẻo lánh và trong nước uống. Giặt quần áo sợi tổng hợp là một nguồn khác, vì mỗi lần giặt có thể thải hàng nghìn sợi vào nước thải.

paragraphs.en: Marine animals frequently mistake these particles for food. Once swallowed, plastic can fill their stomachs without providing any nutrition. Scientists are still investigating the effects on human health, and so far the evidence is limited.
paragraphs.vi: Động vật biển thường nhầm các hạt này là thức ăn. Khi bị nuốt, nhựa có thể lấp đầy dạ dày mà không cung cấp dinh dưỡng. Các nhà khoa học vẫn đang nghiên cứu ảnh hưởng đến sức khoẻ con người và đến nay bằng chứng còn hạn chế.

paragraphs.en: Removing microplastics from the environment is almost impossible, so most experts agree that the priority is prevention: using less single-use plastic, improving waste collection and developing filters for washing machines.
paragraphs.vi: Loại bỏ vi nhựa khỏi môi trường gần như không thể, nên hầu hết chuyên gia đồng ý ưu tiên là phòng ngừa: dùng ít nhựa dùng một lần, cải thiện thu gom rác và phát triển bộ lọc cho máy giặt.

headings: Why prevention matters more than cleaning up
Tiny particles found almost everywhere
What microplastics are and where they come from
Harm to wildlife and open questions about people
New machines that clean plastic from the ocean
Why face scrubs were banned
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 defines microplastics and explains where they come from; paragraph 2 shows how far they travel and names washing as another source; paragraph 3 covers the effects on animals and the limited evidence about humans; paragraph 4 explains why prevention is the priority. Paragraph 4 says removal is almost impossible, and the passage never mentions a ban on face scrubs.

exercises.prompt: Which statement best summarizes the passage?
choices: Microplastics are mainly a problem caused by face scrubs, which are now less common.
Scientists have shown that microplastics are now the biggest threat to human health.
Washing machines are the main source of microplastics, so filters will solve the problem.
Microplastics spread widely and harm wildlife, so preventing them is the priority.
exercises.explain: The passage defines microplastics (paragraph 1), shows how widely they spread (paragraph 2), describes harm to marine animals (paragraph 3) and says prevention is the priority (paragraph 4). Face scrubs and washing are only examples of sources, and paragraph 3 says the evidence on human health is limited.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 3, the word "mistake" is closest in meaning to …
choices: confuse
refuse
search for
notice
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: "Marine animals frequently mistake these particles for food" — they confuse the plastic with food and swallow it.

exercises.prompt: What can be inferred from paragraph 1 about the tiny beads in face scrubs?
choices: They are the main source of microplastics today.
They are less common now than they used to be.
They are larger than five millimeters.
They break down quickly in sea water.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: the beads were "once common in face scrubs", which suggests they are less common now. The same paragraph says most microplastics come from larger items breaking apart, so the beads are not the main source.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer mention deep ocean trenches and remote mountain tops?
choices: To describe where most plastic waste is dumped
To explain where drinking water comes from
To show how far microplastics can travel
To show that microplastics are heavier than expected
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: "Because they are so small and light, microplastics travel easily"; the trenches and mountain tops are examples of how far they reach.

exercises.statement: Swallowed microplastics can fill an animal's stomach without feeding it.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: once swallowed, plastic can fill marine animals' stomachs "without providing any nutrition".

exercises.statement: Scientists have proved that microplastics seriously damage human health.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: scientists are still investigating the effects on human health, and so far the evidence is limited.

exercises.statement: Plastic bottles break apart faster than plastic bags.
exercises.explain: The passage does not compare how fast bottles and bags break apart.

exercises.prompt: Each wash of synthetic clothes can release thousands of ___.
choices: fibers
beads
bottles
exercises.explain: Đoạn 2: "each wash can release thousands of fibers".

exercises.text: Microplastics are plastic fragments under five millimeters long. A few are made at that size on purpose, but most appear as bigger objects gradually ___. Being tiny and light, they spread to places as distant as ocean trenches, and laundry adds more because synthetic clothes shed ___ in the wash. Sea creatures often swallow them as if they were ___, while their effect on people is still unclear. Since cleaning them up is almost impossible, experts focus on ___.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: most microplastics form when larger items break apart; paragraph 2: each wash releases thousands of fibers; paragraph 3: animals mistake them for food; paragraph 4: removal is almost impossible, so the priority is prevention.

lessons.title: Vì sao ta trì hoãn
lessons.summary: Trì hoãn là chuyện cảm xúc hơn là lười biếng.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: Almost everyone has delayed an important task while doing something less useful, such as tidying a desk or scrolling through social media. This is procrastination, and it is commonly blamed on laziness or poor time management.
paragraphs.vi: Hầu như ai cũng từng hoãn một việc quan trọng để làm việc kém hữu ích hơn, như dọn bàn hay lướt mạng xã hội. Đó là trì hoãn và người ta thường đổ lỗi cho sự lười biếng hay quản lý thời gian kém.

paragraphs.en: Many psychologists, however, see it differently. They argue that procrastination is mainly a way of avoiding unpleasant emotions. When a task makes us feel anxious, bored or afraid of failing, putting it off brings immediate relief. Unfortunately, the relief is short-lived, and the task usually becomes more stressful as the deadline approaches.
paragraphs.vi: Tuy nhiên, nhiều nhà tâm lý học nhìn nhận khác. Họ cho rằng trì hoãn chủ yếu là cách né tránh cảm xúc khó chịu. Khi một việc khiến ta lo lắng, chán hay sợ thất bại, hoãn lại đem đến cảm giác nhẹ nhõm tức thì. Tiếc là sự nhẹ nhõm ngắn ngủi và việc thường càng căng thẳng hơn khi hạn chót đến gần.

paragraphs.en: If this view is correct, strict schedules alone will not solve the problem. More helpful strategies include breaking a large task into small, clear steps, starting with just five minutes of work, and treating oneself kindly rather than harshly after falling behind. Research suggests that people who forgive themselves for procrastinating are less likely to do it again.
paragraphs.vi: Nếu quan điểm này đúng, chỉ lịch trình nghiêm ngặt sẽ không giải quyết được vấn đề. Chiến lược hữu ích hơn gồm chia việc lớn thành bước nhỏ rõ ràng, bắt đầu chỉ với năm phút làm việc và đối xử tử tế thay vì khắt khe với bản thân khi bị chậm. Nghiên cứu gợi ý người tha thứ cho mình vì đã trì hoãn ít có khả năng tái phạm hơn.

headings: Practical ways to stop putting things off
A familiar habit with a common explanation
An emotional escape that does not last
Why strict timetables are the best solution
How social media is designed to distract us
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 describes procrastination and the usual explanation (laziness or poor time management); paragraph 2 presents it as an escape from unpleasant emotions that brings only short relief; paragraph 3 suggests practical strategies. Paragraph 3 says strict schedules alone will not solve the problem, and social media is only an example in paragraph 1.

exercises.prompt: What is the main point of the passage?
choices: Procrastination is caused by laziness and can be cured with a stricter daily plan.
Procrastination is mostly emotional, so kind, practical strategies help more than strict schedules.
Social media has become the main reason why people delay important tasks today.
Deadlines make difficult tasks less stressful and easier to finish on time.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2 says many psychologists see procrastination as a way of avoiding unpleasant emotions, and paragraph 3 recommends small steps and self-kindness rather than strict schedules alone. Paragraph 1 mentions laziness only as the common explanation that the passage questions.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 3, the word "harshly" is closest in meaning to …
choices: gently
quickly
severely
secretly
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: "treating oneself kindly rather than harshly" — harshly is the opposite of kindly, so it means severely or strictly.

exercises.prompt: What would the writer most likely say to someone who criticizes themselves after missing a deadline?
choices: Make your schedule even stricter so that it does not happen again.
Accept that you are simply lazy and need much more discipline.
Forget about deadlines, since missing one never has any real cost.
Being kinder to yourself may make you less likely to delay again.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: people who forgive themselves for procrastinating are less likely to do it again, and the writer advises treating oneself kindly rather than harshly. The writer questions both strict schedules alone and the laziness explanation.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer mention tidying a desk in paragraph 1?
choices: To give an example of something less useful done instead of a key task
To recommend tidying as a good way to prepare for important work
To show that people who procrastinate are usually very tidy and organized
To explain how people can manage their time better at their desks
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: people delay an important task "while doing something less useful, such as tidying a desk".

exercises.statement: Feeling bored by a task can lead a person to put it off.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: when a task makes us feel anxious, bored or afraid of failing, putting it off brings immediate relief.

exercises.statement: The relief from putting off a task lasts a long time.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: the relief is short-lived, and the task usually becomes more stressful as the deadline approaches.

exercises.statement: Students procrastinate more than office workers.
exercises.explain: The passage does not compare different groups of people.

exercises.prompt: Breaking a large task into small, clear ___ can help.
choices: steps
days
rules
exercises.explain: Đoạn 3: "breaking a large task into small, clear steps".

exercises.text: People often explain procrastination as ___ or bad planning. Many psychologists, however, believe we delay tasks to escape uncomfortable ___ such as worry or boredom. Putting a task off feels good at first, but the pressure ___ as the deadline gets closer. Instead of relying only on strict timetables, it helps to divide big jobs into smaller parts, begin with a few minutes, and avoid being ___ on yourself.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: procrastination is commonly blamed on laziness; paragraph 2: it is a way of avoiding unpleasant emotions, and the task becomes more stressful as the deadline approaches; paragraph 3: treat yourself kindly rather than harshly.

lessons.title: Du lịch quá tải
lessons.summary: Khi điểm đến bị khách du lịch nhấn chìm.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: Tourism brings money and jobs to many places, but in some popular destinations it has become a source of tension. The term "overtourism" describes situations in which the number of visitors is so high that it damages the environment or the quality of life of local residents.
paragraphs.vi: Du lịch mang tiền và việc làm đến nhiều nơi, nhưng ở một số điểm đến nổi tiếng nó trở thành nguồn căng thẳng. Từ "overtourism" mô tả tình trạng lượng khách quá đông đến mức gây hại cho môi trường hoặc chất lượng sống của cư dân địa phương.

paragraphs.en: The effects are easy to see in small historic towns. Narrow streets become crowded, rents rise as apartments are converted into short-term holiday rentals, and traditional shops are replaced by souvenir stores. Some residents feel that they are being pushed out of their own neighborhoods.
paragraphs.vi: Hậu quả dễ thấy ở các thị trấn cổ nhỏ. Phố hẹp trở nên chật chội, tiền thuê nhà tăng khi căn hộ chuyển thành chỗ cho thuê ngắn hạn, và cửa hàng truyền thống bị thay bằng quầy đồ lưu niệm. Một số cư dân cảm thấy họ đang bị đẩy ra khỏi chính khu phố của mình.

paragraphs.en: Local authorities have tried several solutions. These include daily limits on visitor numbers, tourist taxes, and campaigns that encourage travelers to visit lesser-known areas or come outside the peak season. Results have been mixed, as reducing crowds can also reduce income for businesses that depend on tourists.
paragraphs.vi: Chính quyền địa phương đã thử nhiều giải pháp, gồm giới hạn số khách mỗi ngày, thuế du lịch và chiến dịch khuyến khích du khách đến nơi ít tên tuổi hơn hoặc đi ngoài mùa cao điểm. Kết quả lẫn lộn, vì giảm đám đông cũng có thể giảm thu nhập của các doanh nghiệp sống nhờ khách du lịch.

paragraphs.en: Travelers themselves can help by staying longer in one place, spending money in locally owned businesses and respecting the customs of the communities they visit.
paragraphs.vi: Bản thân du khách có thể giúp bằng cách ở lâu hơn tại một nơi, chi tiêu ở cơ sở do người địa phương làm chủ và tôn trọng phong tục của cộng đồng nơi họ đến.

headings: What visitors themselves can do
When visitors become a burden
How daily life changes for residents
Official responses and their limits
The rise of cheap flights
Why souvenir shops earn the most money
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 defines overtourism as tourism that damages places and residents' lives; paragraph 2 describes its effects on residents in historic towns; paragraph 3 covers the authorities' solutions and their mixed results; paragraph 4 says what travelers can do. Flights and souvenir-shop profits are never discussed.

exercises.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
choices: Why tourism damages every destination and should be strictly limited everywhere
How travelers can find cheap holiday rentals in small and popular historic towns
How too many visitors can harm places and residents, and what can be done about it
How traditional shops in historic towns have changed over the last hundred years
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 defines overtourism, paragraph 2 describes its effects, and paragraphs 3–4 describe what authorities and travelers can do. Paragraph 1 also says tourism brings money and jobs, so it does not damage every destination.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 2, the word "converted" is closest in meaning to …
choices: sold quickly to new owners
changed into something else
repaired and made like new
rented out cheaply to locals
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: "apartments are converted into short-term holiday rentals" — homes are changed into rentals for tourists.

exercises.prompt: What can be inferred about some residents mentioned in paragraph 2?
choices: Most of them now own souvenir stores.
They are pleased that traditional shops are disappearing.
They earn much more from tourism than before.
They may no longer be able to afford to live in their neighborhoods.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: rents rise and some residents feel "pushed out of their own neighborhoods", which suggests that housing is becoming too expensive for them. Nothing suggests they own souvenir stores or welcome the changes.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer point out that reducing crowds can also reduce income?
choices: To explain why the solutions have had mixed results
To argue that tourist taxes should be removed
To show that businesses support daily visitor limits
To suggest that overtourism is not a real problem
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: "Results have been mixed, as reducing crowds can also reduce income for businesses that depend on tourists." The point explains why the measures are only partly successful.

exercises.statement: Some measures try to spread tourists across different places and times of the year.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: campaigns encourage travelers to visit lesser-known areas or to come outside the peak season.

exercises.statement: The writer advises travelers to spend only a short time in each place.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: the writer advises travelers to stay longer in one place.

exercises.statement: Overtourism first became a problem in the 1990s.
exercises.explain: The passage does not say when the problem began.

exercises.prompt: Travelers should respect the ___ of the communities they visit.
choices: customs
prices
borders
exercises.explain: Câu cuối: "respecting the customs of the communities".

exercises.text: Tourism can support local economies, but in some places the sheer number of visitors damages the environment and makes life harder for ___. In small old towns, streets fill up, housing becomes more ___ as flats are turned into holiday lets, and traditional shops give way to souvenir sellers. Authorities have tried visitor caps, special ___ and campaigns to spread tourists out, with mixed success. Visitors can also help by staying longer, supporting ___ businesses and respecting the traditions of their hosts.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: overtourism harms the quality of life of local residents; paragraph 2: rents rise as apartments become holiday rentals; paragraph 3: authorities use daily limits, tourist taxes and campaigns; paragraph 4: travelers can spend money in locally owned businesses.

lessons.title: Rác vũ trụ
lessons.summary: Quỹ đạo quanh Trái Đất đang đông đúc.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: Since the first satellite was launched in the 1950s, humans have sent thousands of objects into orbit around the Earth. Many are still working, providing services such as weather forecasts, navigation and communications. Many others, however, are no longer useful and simply remain in space as debris.
paragraphs.vi: Kể từ khi vệ tinh đầu tiên được phóng vào thập niên 1950, con người đã đưa hàng nghìn vật thể lên quỹ đạo quanh Trái Đất. Nhiều vật thể vẫn hoạt động, cung cấp dịch vụ như dự báo thời tiết, định vị và liên lạc. Nhưng nhiều vật thể khác không còn tác dụng và chỉ nằm lại trong không gian như rác.

paragraphs.en: Space debris includes old satellites, used rocket parts and tiny fragments created when objects collide. Because these pieces travel at extremely high speeds, even a fragment the size of a coin can seriously damage a working satellite or a spacecraft carrying astronauts.
paragraphs.vi: Rác vũ trụ gồm vệ tinh cũ, bộ phận tên lửa đã dùng và mảnh vụn li ti tạo ra khi các vật thể va chạm. Vì chúng bay với tốc độ cực cao, ngay cả một mảnh cỡ đồng xu cũng có thể làm hỏng nặng vệ tinh đang hoạt động hay tàu vũ trụ chở phi hành gia.

paragraphs.en: Experts worry about a chain reaction: each collision produces more fragments, which then increase the chance of further collisions. If this happened on a large scale, some orbits could become too dangerous to use.
paragraphs.vi: Các chuyên gia lo ngại một phản ứng dây chuyền: mỗi va chạm tạo thêm mảnh vụn, làm tăng khả năng va chạm tiếp theo. Nếu điều này xảy ra trên diện rộng, một số quỹ đạo có thể trở nên quá nguy hiểm để sử dụng.

paragraphs.en: Engineers are now designing satellites that can lower themselves into the atmosphere and burn up at the end of their lives, and testing methods to capture larger pieces of debris. International cooperation will be essential, since no single country owns space.
paragraphs.vi: Kỹ sư hiện đang thiết kế vệ tinh có thể tự hạ xuống bầu khí quyển và cháy rụi khi hết tuổi thọ, đồng thời thử nghiệm cách thu gom các mảnh rác lớn. Hợp tác quốc tế sẽ là thiết yếu vì không quốc gia nào sở hữu không gian.

headings: The risk of a spiral of collisions
Engineering fixes and shared responsibility
The first satellite of the 1950s
Small pieces, serious damage
A crowded orbit of working and abandoned objects
Why astronauts are refusing to fly
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: thousands of objects orbit the Earth, some working and many now debris; paragraph 2: what debris is and why even tiny pieces are dangerous; paragraph 3: the fear of a chain reaction of collisions; paragraph 4: engineering solutions and international cooperation. The first satellite is only a detail, and astronauts refusing to fly is never mentioned.

exercises.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Satellites are no longer needed for weather forecasts, navigation and communications.
Growing debris threatens the use of orbit, and solving it needs new technology and cooperation.
Space debris is mainly a danger to people and buildings on the ground below it.
One wealthy country has already taken full responsibility for cleaning up space.
exercises.explain: Paragraphs 1–3 describe the growing debris and the danger of collisions, and paragraph 4 describes engineering solutions and the need for international cooperation. Paragraph 1 says many satellites still provide useful services, and paragraph 4 says no single country owns space.

exercises.prompt: Why can a coin-sized fragment be dangerous?
choices: It travels at extremely high speeds.
It gives off harmful radiation in space.
It is made of unusually heavy metal.
It blocks the radio signals of satellites.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: because these pieces travel at extremely high speeds, even a fragment the size of a coin can seriously damage a satellite or spacecraft.

exercises.prompt: What is the "chain reaction" experts worry about?
choices: Satellites stop working one after another.
Rockets become more expensive.
Collisions create fragments that cause more collisions.
Countries compete to launch more satellites.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: each collision produces more fragments, which then increase the chance of further collisions.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 4, the word "essential" is closest in meaning to …
choices: optional
expensive
difficult
necessary
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: "International cooperation will be essential, since no single country owns space" — cooperation is necessary because no country can act alone.

exercises.prompt: What can be inferred about satellites designed to lower themselves into the atmosphere?
choices: They travel more slowly than other satellites while in orbit.
They will not remain as debris after they stop working.
They are designed to be used only for weather forecasts.
They can also capture larger pieces of debris in orbit.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: these satellites burn up at the end of their lives, so they will not remain in space as debris (paragraph 1). Capturing larger pieces is a separate method mentioned in the same paragraph.

exercises.statement: All objects sent into orbit are still working.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: many objects are no longer useful and simply remain in space as debris.

exercises.statement: Cleaning up space debris will be paid for by private companies.
exercises.explain: The passage does not say who will pay for cleaning up space debris.

exercises.prompt: International ___ will be essential, since no single country owns space.
choices: cooperation
competition
tourism
exercises.explain: Câu cuối: "International cooperation will be essential".

exercises.text: Since the 1950s, thousands of objects have been sent into orbit; many still provide useful ___, but many others are now just junk. This junk includes old satellites, rocket parts and small fragments produced by ___. Even a coin-sized piece can do serious harm because of its enormous ___. Experts fear that each crash could create more pieces and eventually make some orbits ___. Engineers are working on solutions, but no nation can solve the problem alone.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: working satellites provide services such as weather forecasts and navigation; paragraph 2: fragments are created when objects collide, and they are dangerous because of their extremely high speeds; paragraph 3: some orbits could become too dangerous to use.
